pdfkb.name: Compress PDF to Exact Size
pdfkb.short: Shrink a PDF to a target size like 100 KB, 200 KB or 1 MB.
pdfkb.title: Compress PDF to KB or MB – Exact Target Size | {brand}
pdfkb.desc: Compress a PDF to an exact size such as 100 KB, 200 KB, 500 KB or 1 MB. Free, no upload, no sign-up – it runs in your browser.
pdfkb.h1: Compress PDF to a target size
steps: Choose the PDF you need to make smaller.
Enter the target size and pick KB or MB.
Click Start – the tool tries the gentlest method first and downloads the largest file that fits.

faq.q: How does it hit an exact size?
faq.a: It works in stages. First a lossless rebuild, then images are recompressed at steadily lower resolution and quality while text stays vector. Only if that is not enough does it turn pages into images, searching resolution and quality until the file is just under your limit.

faq.q: Is my PDF uploaded?
faq.a: No. Everything happens on your device, so confidential documents never leave it. You can even switch off Wi-Fi after the page loads.

faq.q: What if the target is impossible?
faq.a: You get the smallest file that could be produced and a clear warning, so you can split the PDF or remove pages instead.

faq.q: Will text still be selectable?
faq.a: Yes whenever image recompression alone reaches the target. If pages have to be rasterized, untick the option to keep text and accept a larger file.

faq.q: KB or kB?
faq.a: The tool uses 1 KB = 1024 bytes, which matches how Windows and most portals measure. Enter a slightly lower number if a portal uses 1000.

faq.q: Is there a page or file limit?
faq.a: No hourly or daily limits. Very large PDFs are limited only by your device memory.

faq.q: Does it work on phones?
faq.a: Yes, on Android and iPhone browsers. Big scans are faster on a laptop.

faq.q: Is it really free?
faq.a: Yes – no watermark, no account, no trial.

guide.intro: Most PDF compressors give you vague levels like ‘low’ or ‘high’ and leave you to guess whether the result will pass a portal’s size check. {brand} lets you type the limit itself – 100 KB, 250 KB, 1 MB – and does the trial and error for you, entirely in your browser.
uses: Meet upload limits on job, exam, visa and admission portals.
Fit attachments under email and helpdesk limits.
Shrink scanned documents from phone scanner apps.
Prepare court, tax and insurance e-filing documents.
tips: Remove blank or unnecessary pages first with Delete pages.
Scan in grayscale – it is much smaller than colour.
Aim 5–10% below the limit to allow for how a portal counts bytes.
If you must keep text selectable, set a slightly larger target.
more: The three stages

Stage one rebuilds the file losslessly and removes junk. Stage two decodes every photo or scan inside the PDF and re-encodes it as JPEG, stepping from 2000 px at high quality down to about 400 px, checking the size each time. Stage three renders every page as an image and searches combinations of resolution (from about 144 dpi down to about 30 dpi) and JPEG quality, keeping the largest result that fits, so you get the best quality the limit allows.
Why some PDFs barely shrink

A PDF made purely of text and vector graphics is already compact; most of its size is fonts. Such files rarely need compressing, and rasterizing them can even make them bigger. Scans and photo-heavy files, on the other hand, can usually shrink by 80–95%.

faq.q: Can I compress several PDFs to this size?
faq.a: Run each file in turn – there is no queue or wait, and no limit on how many.

faq.q: Should I use this or the regular Compress PDF tool?
faq.a: Use this page when a form states a maximum size. Use Compress PDF when you just want a smaller file with the best quality.

steps: Select the PDF you need to upload.
The target is preset to 100 KB – change it if your form needs a different size.
Click Start and download a PDF under the limit.

faq.q: How do I compress a PDF to 100 KB?
faq.a: Open the file here and press Start. The size box is already set to 100 KB; the tool tries image recompression first and rasterizes pages only if needed, then shows the final size.

faq.q: Will a 100 KB PDF still be readable?
faq.a: At 100 KB a multi-page scan usually needs page rasterizing at around 70–100 dpi; one or two text pages often fit with text kept sharp.

faq.q: Is my document uploaded anywhere?
faq.a: No. Compression runs on your device; nothing is sent to a server.

faq.q: What if it cannot reach the size?
faq.a: You will get the smallest version possible and a warning. Split the PDF or remove pages, then try again.

faq.q: Does the portal count 1 KB as 1000 or 1024 bytes?
faq.a: Most count 1024. If yours rejects the file, set the target a few KB lower.

faq.q: Is there a daily limit?
faq.a: No limits, no watermark, no account.
